brief.headline: Todd Boehly's Eldridge builds and holds sports and youth media businesses, and its recent Overtime deal and 25-29 fan overlap make a fan-night app a plausible strategic fit, though Eldridge does control and minority deals rather than venture rounds.
brief.angle: Position the startup as a fan-engagement platform that extends the sports and youth media fan relationship into the live night out, with a clear path to a larger consolidated consumer platform. Frame the ask as a strategic or minority conversation, not a seed round, and lead with how the product deepens fan loyalty for properties Eldridge already touches.

name_drop.line: Eldridge Capital led a strategic round in Overtime in September 2026, and we are building the in-person side of the same youth fan relationship: the night out after the screen.
name_drop.name: Overtime

name_drop.line: Our users over-index on Los Angeles Dodgers fandom, so pre-game and post-game routines around games are exactly where we add value.
name_drop.name: Los Angeles Dodgers

name_drop.line: Our customers' affinity for Chelsea F.C. is strong, and we turn that match-day energy into a full night with bars, merch and rides.
name_drop.name: Chelsea F.C.

deck: Lead with retention and repeat behaviour among 25-29 year olds, since their portfolio and your crowd share that age band.
Show the sports and youth media fan overlap with your customer data, using the affinity scores for Overtime, Los Angeles Dodgers and Chelsea F.C.
Explain the three revenue lines (pre-show bars, merch, rides) and how each one grows with event frequency per fan.
Position Ticketmaster, Spotify and Uber as reference points for how a fan platform becomes a daily habit, and state clearly where you are different.
Include a slide on how you would fit inside a consolidated platform, such as shared fan data or partner distribution, without implying a credit or insurance link.

openers.line: How do you see sports media platforms like Bleacher Report turning fan attention into repeat, paid behaviour?
openers.name: Bleacher Report

openers.line: What makes game-day rituals stick for a club like the Golden State Warriors, and where do those rituals fall short?
openers.name: Golden State Warriors

openers.line: When a brand like Nike thinks about fans before an event, where does the experience usually break down?
openers.name: Nike

avoid: Do not pitch this as a venture-stage seed round, since Eldridge's stated approach is control, acquisition and minority-stake deals.
Do not claim Todd Boehly personally loves any of these properties; the common-ground list reflects what fans of his public interests also enjoy.
Do not lead with credit, insurance or asset management themes, since your startup has no link to them and it will read as a mismatch.
questions: What size of stake or level of control would you consider in a company at this stage, and would you take a minority position?
How would a live-events app fit alongside Overtime and your other sports and media holdings, and what would the strategic rationale be?
What is your take rate on pre-show bars, merch and rides, and how does per-fan spend change across repeat events?

picks.line: We're building the night-out layer around the ticket the way on-demand delivery reshaped everyday errands, so fans can get drinks and merch delivered or picked up before doors open.
Fan identity drives how people spend around an event, and we're designing each fanbase's pre-show experience to match the community norms that Cloud9 has built around its audience.
Overtime has shown how much engagement a young fanbase will give a brand that speaks its language, and we're applying that same approach to the hours around a concert.

openers.line: Fans already book the ticket on Ticketmaster and the ride on Uber, but nobody owns the hours in between, and that's the gap we're filling.
A concert is one of the few times a fan spends a full evening with a community, so we built an app that turns the ticket into the whole night out.
